% Research-only P06.1 candidate, 30 August 2026.
% Not included by the live manuscript.  No novelty or priority claim is made.

\begin{lemma}
\label{lem:p061-product-open-tube}
Let \(K\) be a complete non-Archimedean field with nontrivial absolute
value.  Let \(A\) and \(B\) be strict \(K\)-affinoid algebras, let
\(a\in\mathcal M(A)(K)\), and write
\[
 P=A\widehat\otimes_KB,
 \qquad
 s_a:\mathcal M(B)\longrightarrow\mathcal M(P)
\]
for the section induced by evaluation at \(a\).  If
\(z\in\mathcal M(B)\) and \(\Omega\subset\mathcal M(P)\) is an ordinary
open neighbourhood of \(s_a(z)\), then there are strict affinoid
neighbourhoods \(U\subset\mathcal M(A)\) of \(a\) and
\(V\subset\mathcal M(B)\) of \(z\) such that
\[
                         U\times_KV\subset\Omega.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proposition}
\label{prop:p061-parameterized-toric-fixed-fibre}
Let \(K\) be as above, let \(N\) be a lattice, put \(M=N^\vee\), and let
\(\rho\subset N_{\mathbf R}\) be a full-dimensional strongly convex
rational polyhedral cone.  Put
\[
 S=\rho^\vee\cap M,
 \qquad
 Z=\operatorname{Spec}K[S],
\]
and denote by \(a\in Z^{\mathrm{an}}(K)\) its torus-fixed point.  Let \(Y\)
be a good strict \(K\)-analytic space, let \(y\in Y\), and let
\(\Omega\) be an ordinary open neighbourhood of \((a,y)\) in
\(Z^{\mathrm{an}}\times_KY\).  For every classically pluriharmonic
function \(h:\Omega\to\mathbf R\), there are strict affinoid
neighbourhoods \(U\) of \(a\) and \(V\) of \(y\), with
\(U\times_KV\subset\Omega\), such that
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p061-parameterized-toric-factorization}
 h|_{U\times_KV}
   =p_V^*g,
 \qquad
 g=s_a^*h|_V\in\operatorname{PH}(V).
\end{equation}
The neighbourhood \(U\) can be chosen from the cofinal weighted toric
affinoids
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p061-parameterized-weighted-domain}
 U_n=\left\{x\in Z^{\mathrm{an}}:
  |\chi^u(x)|\leq|\varpi|^{n\langle u,v\rangle}
  \text{ for every }u\in S\right\},
\end{equation}
where \(0<|\varpi|<1\) and \(v\in N\cap\operatorname{int}(\rho)\).
In particular, if \(Y\) has the local property that every classically
pluriharmonic function is \(\mathbf R\)-PL, then the germ of \(h\) at
\((a,y)\) is \(\mathbf R\)-PL.  This applies when \(Y\) is quasi-smooth.
\end{proposition}

\begin{theorem}
\label{thm:p061-split-toric-all-orbits}
Let \(K\) be a complete non-Archimedean field with nontrivial absolute
value, let \(N\) be a lattice, and let
\(\sigma\subset N_{\mathbf R}\) be any strongly convex rational
polyhedral cone, with no simpliciality or full-dimensionality assumption.
Set
\[
 X_\sigma=\operatorname{Spec}
 K[\sigma^\vee\cap M],
 \qquad M=N^\vee.
\]
Every classically pluriharmonic function on an ordinary open analytic
subspace \(W\subset X_\sigma^{\mathrm{an}}\) is \(\mathbf R\)-PL and
harmonic in the sense of Gubler--Jell--Rabinoff.  Equivalently, this holds
at every analytic point of every torus orbit, including every
positive-dimensional orbit of a non-simplicial cone.
\end{theorem}

\begin{corollary}
\label{cor:p061-split-toric-varieties}
The conclusion of \Cref{thm:p061-split-toric-all-orbits} holds on every
ordinary open analytic subspace of the analytification of a split toric
variety associated to an arbitrary fan.  It also holds on every good
strict analytic space which is analytically locally isomorphic to an
ordinary open neighbourhood of a point
\[
 (a,y)\in Z^{\mathrm{an}}\times_KY,
\]
where \(Z\) and \(a\) are as in
\Cref{prop:p061-parameterized-toric-fixed-fibre} and \(Y\) is
quasi-smooth.
\end{corollary}

\begin{corollary}
\label{cor:p061-toric-forms}
Let \(X\) be a \(K\)-variety for which there is a finite analytic field
extension \(L/K\) such that \(X_L\) is a split toric \(L\)-variety.  Then
every classically pluriharmonic function on an ordinary open analytic
subspace of \(X^{\mathrm{an}}\) is \(\mathbf R\)-PL and
Gubler--Jell--Rabinoff harmonic.  In particular, the conclusion holds for
ordinary open subspaces of algebraic toric forms after any finite field
extension which splits the form.
\end{corollary}

# P06.1: all torus orbits of a split toric variety

Research-only dossier, 30 August 2026.  It is not a live-book input and
has not been sent to production Rethlas.  No novelty or priority claim is
made.

## Result isolated

The packet proves a parameterized strengthening of the already verified
toric-fixed-point theorem.  Near the fixed section of a product
`(full-dimensional affine toric cone) × Y`, every classically
pluriharmonic function is pulled back from `Y`.  The proof tests every
actual Berkovich fibre over its completed residue field.  The weighted
semigroup affinoid in that fibre has canonical reduction
`\widetilde{\mathscr H(y)}[S]`, an integral domain, and hence singleton
Shilov boundary.  The affinoid maximum--minimum principle forces fibrewise
constancy.

Every orbit of an arbitrary split affine toric variety has a principal
open neighbourhood

`X_tau × T`

where `tau` is full-dimensional in its saturated span, `X_tau` is viewed at
its torus-fixed point, and `T` is a split torus.  Applying the parameterized
statement and the verified quasi-smooth P06.1 theorem on `T` proves
classically pluriharmonic implies real-PL at every orbit, without
simpliciality.  Fan gluing gives arbitrary split toric varieties.  Finite
scalar extension plus GJR ground-field descent gives every toric form which
becomes split over a finite analytic field extension.

## Exact dependency audit

- Gubler--Rabinoff, *Classically psh and pluriharmonic functions on
  Berkovich spaces*, arXiv:2506.13548v2, local PDF SHA-256
  `83ca9a19394f44bb2e4e1aa316de95938f311acd53a00fe250fa0f605184b726`.
  The packet uses Proposition 7.2(6),(7), Proposition 7.3, and Theorem 4.3
  in their stated directions.
- Gubler--Jell--Rabinoff, *Forms on Berkovich spaces based on harmonic
  tropicalizations*, audited PDF SHA-256
  `572d51c9f8907dbb814684f7d136612243c0e0b70cddbe6759bb686f0bcfbd42`.
  The packet uses Definition 5.1, Section 5.2(4), Lemma 5.4(1), Corollary
  5.12, and Definition 7.2.
- The rational-section tube statement/proof already passed production with
  exact SHA-256
  `96b246d6f6032bce38751095935525a67456c6753e006e7b188778bc945e50bc`
  and
  `6f6158b5253922539f81e42ab9e6d9e2c48a6b3c8b727e4157351b9591baabe5`.
  The present packet repeats the needed ordinary-open part so that its
  logical core is self-contained.
- The toric fixed-point statement/proof already passed production with
  exact SHA-256
  `edbe69950a0a9c81ca2fd9077a58be96ec6bdb6c27ce9cf2524da5bf653a5ab6`
  and
  `531e326b4aeb19067fcb88af2f6eb6477a169587d71a3249103777c9131cf8f4`.
  The present proof strengthens it by proving singleton Shilov boundary
  after scalar extension to every completed residue field and applying it
  fibrewise.
- The quasi-smooth P06.1 statement/proof used on the orbit torus have
  exact SHA-256
  0b1b4d161e3b85d342d7be88234a8ed27bfe74be4d24a639ff0456373a7a39e9
  and
  fdc6abcc4988644656892172fbdbda4178cb86ca710fd0122a90947e598b0b8b.

## Independent research audit

An independent hostile audit of the exact statement and proof returned
PASS, with no counterexample, fatal gap, or hidden hypothesis.  It checked
the completed-residue-field fibres, geometric singleton Shilov boundary,
ordinary-open tube, all face extremes and non-full-dimensional cones,
the exact localized-monoid product chart, and finite scalar descent.
Its three optional exposition suggestions (closed immersion for the
affinoid domain, analytic/topological fibre identification, and rational
relative-interior positivity) have been incorporated into the frozen text.
This is a research audit only, not production Rethlas verification.

## Hostile checks

1. **No product-topology shortcut.**  The open-tube lemma is proved using
   upper and lower inequalities in the Berkovich topology and a completed
   tensor-product kernel estimate.
2. **No rigid-point density.**  Fibrewise constancy is proved over
   `\mathscr H(b)` for every `b` in the parameter affinoid.
3. **Geometric Shilov issue.**  Singleton Shilov boundary is reproved after
   every analytic extension, using the domain
   `\widetilde{\mathscr H(b)}[S]`.
4. **No simplicial cover.**  The orbit chart is an exact localization of
   monoids.  It works for a non-simplicial face because the transverse cone
   is merely full-dimensional in its saturated span.
5. **No false descent along a proper modification.**  No toric resolution,
   alteration, normalization, or nonflat finite descent occurs.
6. **Actual scope.**  The theorem concerns ordinary open analytic
   subspaces.  It does not assert the result at a relative-boundary point of
   an arbitrary analytic domain unless that domain has the displayed local
   product chart.

## Fail-closed residual boundary

This packet does **not** prove P06.1 for a general toroidal or log-etale
chart.  A genuine log-etale chart need not be an analytic local
isomorphism to the product in the proposition.  The fibrewise argument
needs an actual analytic projection whose transverse fibres are the
weighted cone affinoids.  Pullback along a log-etale or ordinary etale map
does not supply such a projection, and the currently verified PL descent
theorems do not descend an arbitrary PL function through a proper toric
modification or a general nonflat alteration.

The next minimal atom is therefore:

> Let `q: X -> Z × Y` be an ordinary etale (or strict log-etale) chart,
> with `Z` a full-dimensional split affine toric cone, and let `x` lie over
> the fixed stratum.  Prove that, after an etale cover of a neighbourhood of
> `x`, the chart admits a product projection with singleton-Shilov
> transverse fibres; or construct a classically pluriharmonic function
> showing that this relative product assertion is false.

Until that local-product assertion is proved, the general toroidal/log-etale
claim must remain open.  The arbitrary nonproduct singular analytic germ
residual is unchanged.

# Independent hostile-audit receipt: P06.1 all toric orbits

Date: 30 August 2026  
Audit role: independent hostile mathematical audit  
Disposition: research-only; no production Rethlas call was made

## Exact audited bytes

- Statement: `p061_all_toric_orbits_statement_20260830.tex`  
  SHA-256: `05bda70eb1cf7ebbcc95d1831feadd946afa168f64a7298171381b9f1e865e60`
- Proof: `p061_all_toric_orbits_proof_20260830.tex`  
  SHA-256: `21c44c47a91a28469fb91a6c00569ed56d12699bae9c956c68c33ad493825b03`

For identification only, the accompanying dossier audited with those files was
`p061_all_toric_orbits_dossier_20260830.md`, SHA-256
`f88eaa16cfeff0ee66f00a336ac10e24d49b0b1acf06a2cf844ca78ec77dad4a`.

## Verdict

**PASS.**  The exact statement and proof bytes above have **0 critical
findings and 0 mathematical gaps**.  No counterexample was found within the
stated hypotheses.  The argument does not use a simplicial alteration, proper
descent, rigid-point density, or a product-topology shortcut.

## Obligations checked

### 1. Ordinary-open product tube

- The section is defined by a genuinely `K`-rational point, so evaluation has
  values in `K` and gives the bounded retraction
  `A completed-tensor B -> B` used in the proof.
- For a kernel element, finite tensors are dense.  Subtracting the evaluated
  tensor keeps the approximation arbitrarily close and makes every first
  factor vanish at the rational point.
- Nontriviality of the absolute value supplies strict rational neighbourhoods
  on which finitely many such factors are uniformly small.
- Upper and lower basic-open inequalities are both preserved.  In the lower
  inequalities the perturbation is strictly smaller than the evaluated term,
  so the ultrametric equality, not an Archimedean estimate, gives the desired
  inclusion.
- Thus the proof produces an actual affinoid product inside an ordinary open
  neighbourhood; it does not assume that the underlying Berkovich product has
  the ordinary product topology.

### 2. Weighted transverse toric domains

- Full dimensionality and strong convexity imply that every nonzero element
  of `S=rho^vee intersect M` has strictly positive pairing with the chosen
  integral interior vector.
- Finite generation of `S` reduces the displayed infinite family of bounds to
  finitely many strict Weierstrass bounds.  Rescaling is compatible with all
  monoid relations.
- The domains are nested strict affinoid neighbourhoods of the rational fixed
  point.  Their intersection is exactly that point.
- Compactness of the first domain and the nested-closed-set argument prove
  cofinality among ordinary neighbourhoods; no first-countability assumption
  is used.

### 3. Every completed-residue-field fibre

- For an arbitrary Berkovich parameter point `b`, the analytic fibre is the
  scalar extension of the weighted toric domain to `H(b)`.
- Extending the function first to `H(b)` and then pulling it back along the
  canonical `H(b)`-rational lift of `b` is legitimate by the cited scalar
  extension and functoriality assertions for classical pluriharmonicity.
- The fibre algebra is exactly the semigroup Tate algebra
  `H(b)<S>` after the displayed integral rescaling.  It remains strict over
  `H(b)` because the radii come from `|K^times|`.
- A nonzero convergent semigroup series attains its Gauss norm at a
  coefficient.  Hence it can be normalized to norm one.  The product of two
  nonzero reductions is nonzero in
  `tilde(H(b))[S]`, which embeds in the group algebra
  `tilde(H(b))[M]`.  This proves multiplicativity of the Gauss norm.
- The Gauss norm is therefore the supremum norm and the canonical reduction is
  the integral domain `tilde(H(b))[S]`.  The Shilov boundary consists of its
  single semigroup Gauss point.
- The maximum and minimum of the pulled-back pluriharmonic function occur at
  this one point, so they are equal and the function is constant on the whole
  analytic fibre.
- The analytic fibre over `b` identifies with the full topological fibre of
  the projection.  Since `b` was arbitrary, this proves pointwise
  factorization through the parameter, including all non-rigid product
  points.

### 4. Orbit principal-open product decomposition

- Every analytic point has a unique torus-orbit face via its scheme-theoretic
  support.
- `N_tau=N intersect span_R(tau)` is saturated, hence admits a lattice
  complement.
- Rationality of the dual face supplies an integral relative-interior element
  `q`.  It vanishes on `tau` and is strictly positive on every ray outside
  `tau`.
- Localizing at `chi^q` gives exactly
  `{m in M : m restricted to tau is nonnegative}`: adding a sufficiently large
  multiple of `q` corrects all finitely many inequalities outside `tau` and
  leaves those on `tau` unchanged.
- Under any chosen lattice splitting this monoid is the direct sum of the
  dual monoid of `tau` in its saturated span and the character lattice of the
  complementary torus.  Therefore the asserted algebraic product chart is
  exact.
- The check includes `tau=0`, `tau=sigma`, non-full-dimensional `sigma`,
  positive-dimensional orbits, and nonsimplicial faces.  In the transverse
  lattice, `tau` is full-dimensional and has the rational torus-fixed point
  required by the parameterized proposition.

### 5. Passage to real-PL and harmonicity

- The parameter factor is an affinoid domain of a split torus and hence
  quasi-smooth.  The already verified quasi-smooth P06.1 result makes the
  factor real-PL.
- Pullback stability and sheafiness yield real-PL regularity near every point
  and then on the whole ordinary open subspace.
- Classical pluriharmonicity gives classical psh for both signs.  The cited
  comparison for real-PL functions makes both signs semipositive, which is the
  asserted Gubler--Jell--Rabinoff harmonicity.

### 6. Split fans and nonsplit forms

- Affine toric charts cover a split toric variety, so the affine conclusion
  glues by sheafiness.
- For a finite analytic extension splitting the variety, scalar extension
  preserves classical pluriharmonicity and inverse images of ordinary opens
  remain ordinary open.
- The split theorem applies upstairs and the cited ground-field descent for
  real-PL functions returns the conclusion over `K`.  The original function
  and its negative are still classically psh, so harmonicity follows from the
  same comparison theorem downstairs.

## Noncritical presentation notes

The proof is already complete.  Three optional reader-facing additions would
only make implicit standard facts explicit: mention the closed immersion
defined by finite monoid generators when introducing the weighted affinoids;
cite the standard identification of an analytic fibre with the corresponding
topological fibre; and state that rationality of the dual face supplies the
integral relative-interior point.  None is a missing mathematical step.

## Scope firewall

This receipt validates only the following scope of the frozen bytes:

- ordinary open analytic subspaces of arbitrary split toric varieties;
- every orbit, including positive-dimensional orbits of nonsimplicial cones
  and cones that are not full-dimensional;
- actual analytic local product models consisting of a full-dimensional
  split affine toric fixed-point factor and a quasi-smooth factor; and
- varieties which become split toric after the finite analytic field
  extension used in the statement.

It does **not** validate or assert the theorem for a general toroidal space, a
genuine log-etale chart, an arbitrary analytic domain at a relative-boundary
point, a nonsplit local model without a splitting analytic extension, or an
arbitrary nonproduct singular analytic germ.  It supplies no descent through
a proper toric modification or a general nonflat alteration.  Those cases
remain outside this packet.

% Research-only source-aware proof for P06.1, 30 August 2026.
% Not included by the live manuscript.  No novelty or priority claim is made.

\begin{proof}[Proof of \Cref{lem:p061-product-open-tube}]
Let
\[
 \epsilon=\epsilon_a\widehat\otimes1:P\longrightarrow B.
\]
We first record the elementary uniform estimate used below.  If
\(G\in\ker\epsilon\) and \(\eta>0\), there is a strict affinoid
neighbourhood \(U\) of \(a\) such that
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p061-product-kernel-small}
       \sup_{U\times_K\mathcal M(B)}|G|<\eta.
\end{equation}
Indeed, choose a finite tensor
\(T=\sum_{i=1}^r a_i\otimes b_i\) sufficiently close to \(G\), and put
\[
                  b_0=\epsilon(T)\in B.
\]
Boundedness of \(\epsilon\) and the equality \(\epsilon(G)=0\) make
\(\lVert b_0\rVert\) arbitrarily small with the approximation error.
Replacing \(T\) by
\[
 T-1\otimes b_0
   =\sum_{i=1}^r(a_i-a_i(a))\otimes b_i
\]
therefore still gives an arbitrarily close approximation.  Every
\(a_i-a_i(a)\) vanishes at
\(a\).  Nontriviality of the valuation supplies arbitrarily small strict
rational neighbourhoods on which all of them have the required small
supremum norm.  The ultrametric inequality proves
\eqref{eq:p061-product-kernel-small}.

Choose a basic ordinary neighbourhood of \(s_a(z)\), contained in
\(\Omega\), of the form
\[
 \Omega_0=
 \bigcap_{i=1}^r\{|F_i|<c_i\}
 \cap
 \bigcap_{j=1}^s\{|H_j|>d_j\},
 \qquad F_i,H_j\in P.
\]
Choose numbers
\[
 |\epsilon(F_i)(z)|<c_i'<c_i,
 \qquad
 d_j<d_j'<|\epsilon(H_j)(z)|.
\]
After shrinking to one strict affinoid neighbourhood \(V\) of \(z\), the
same strict inequalities hold throughout \(V\).  Write, for every
\(L\in\{F_i,H_j\}\),
\[
        L=1\otimes\epsilon(L)+
          \bigl(L-1\otimes\epsilon(L)\bigr).
\]
The second summand belongs to \(\ker\epsilon\).  Apply
\eqref{eq:p061-product-kernel-small} simultaneously, with error smaller
than \(c_i\) for \(F_i\) and smaller than \(d_j'\) for \(H_j\).  On the
resulting \(U\times_KV\), the upper inequalities follow from the
ultrametric triangle inequality.  In the lower inequalities the error is
strictly smaller than \(|\epsilon(H_j)|\), so
\[
                     |H_j|=|\epsilon(H_j)|>d_j'>d_j.
\]
Thus \(U\times_KV\subset\Omega_0\subset\Omega\).
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of
\Cref{prop:p061-parameterized-toric-fixed-fibre}]
Choose \(0<|\varpi|<1\) and
\(v\in N\cap\operatorname{int}(\rho)\), and put
\(\ell(u)=\langle u,v\rangle\).  The weighted domains \(U_n\) in
\eqref{eq:p061-parameterized-weighted-domain} are strict affinoid
neighbourhoods of \(a\): for finite monoid generators
\(u_1,\ldots,u_r\) of \(S\), the corresponding monomials give a closed
immersion \(Z\hookrightarrow\mathbf A_K^r\), and \(U_n\) is the inverse
image of the strict closed polydisc
\[
             |\chi^{u_i}|\leq
             |\varpi|^{n\ell(u_i)}
             \qquad(1\leq i\leq r).
\]
After rescaling the generators, their affinoid algebras are
\(K\langle S\rangle\) with the semigroup Gauss norm.  They are nested,
and
\[
                         \bigcap_{n\geq1}U_n=\{a\}.
\]
The compactness argument for nested closed subsets shows that they are
cofinal among ordinary neighbourhoods of \(a\).  More explicitly, if an
ordinary neighbourhood \(E\) of \(a\) contained no \(U_n\), the nonempty
closed subsets \(U_n\setminus E\) of the compact space \(U_1\) would have
nonempty intersection, contradicting the displayed identity.

Choose strict affinoid neighbourhoods \(A_0\) of \(a\) in
\(Z^{\mathrm{an}}\) and \(B_0\) of \(y\) in \(Y\).  By
\Cref{lem:p061-product-open-tube}, after shrinking there are strict
affinoid neighbourhoods \(A_1\subset A_0\) and \(V\subset B_0\) such
that
\[
                         A_1\times_KV\subset\Omega.
\]
Since \(A_1\) is a neighbourhood of \(a\), choose \(n\) with
\(U_n\subset A_1\).  It remains to prove that \(h\) is constant on every
fibre of
\[
                    p_V:U_n\times_KV\longrightarrow V.
\]
We do this over the actual completed residue field of an arbitrary point,
so no density or rigid-point argument is hidden.  Fix \(b\in V\).  The
analytic fibre is
\[
 (U_n)_{\mathscr H(b)}=
 U_n\widehat\otimes_K\mathscr H(b).
\]
After the rescaling
\(Z^u=\varpi^{-n\ell(u)}\chi^u\), its affinoid algebra is the semigroup
Tate algebra
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p061-basechanged-semigroup-tate}
 \mathscr H(b)\langle S\rangle=
 \left\{\sum_{u\in S}c_uZ^u:
 c_u\in\mathscr H(b),\ |c_u|\longrightarrow0
 \text{ off finite subsets of }S\right\}
\end{equation}
with Gauss norm \(\max_u|c_u|\).  The Gauss norm is multiplicative: after
normalizing two nonzero series to norm one, their nonzero reductions have
nonzero product in the domain
\(\widetilde{\mathscr H(b)}[S]\subset
 \widetilde{\mathscr H(b)}[M]\).  It is therefore the supremum norm, and
the canonical reduction of \eqref{eq:p061-basechanged-semigroup-tate} is
\[
                       \widetilde{\mathscr H(b)}[S].
\]
This is an integral domain.  Hence
the Gauss norm defines a point \(\eta_{n,b}\) of
\((U_n)_{\mathscr H(b)}\), and
\[
        |f(\eta_{n,b})|=\lVert f\rVert_{\mathrm G}
                       =\sup_{(U_n)_{\mathscr H(b)}}|f|
        \qquad
        \bigl(f\in\mathscr H(b)\langle S\rangle\bigr).
\]
Thus \(\{\eta_{n,b}\}\) is itself a boundary.  The nonempty minimal
Shilov boundary is consequently the singleton
\(\{\eta_{n,b}\}\).

First extend \(h\) from \(K\) to \(\mathscr H(b)\); this preserves
classical pluriharmonicity in both directions by
\cite[Proposition~7.2(6)]{GR25Classical}.  The point \(b\) induces an
\(\mathscr H(b)\)-rational point of \(V_{\mathscr H(b)}\), and the
corresponding fibre inclusion
\[
 (U_n)_{\mathscr H(b)}
 \longrightarrow (U_n\times_KV)_{\mathscr H(b)}
\]
is an \(\mathscr H(b)\)-analytic morphism.  Arbitrary pullback preserves
classical pluriharmonicity by
\cite[Proposition~7.2(7)]{GR25Classical}.  Thus the resulting pullback
\(h_b\) is pluriharmonic on the fibre.  The affinoid maximum--minimum
principle \cite[Proposition~7.3]{GR25Classical} says that both extrema of
\(h_b\) occur on its singleton Shilov boundary, so \(h_b\) is constant.
By the standard description of analytic fibres
\cite[\S2.7]{GR25Classical}, the underlying topological space of
\((U_n)_{\mathscr H(b)}\) identifies with the set-theoretic fibre
\(p_V^{-1}(b)\).  Hence every point of \(U_n\times_KV\) belongs to
exactly one of the analytic fibres just treated.  Its value under \(h\)
consequently equals the value at the toric-fixed section in that fibre.
This proves the pointwise identity
\[
              h|_{U_n\times_KV}=p_V^*(s_a^*h|_V).
\]
The function \(g=s_a^*h|_V\) is classically pluriharmonic by the same
functorial pullback result.  If pluriharmonic functions on \(Y\) are locally
\(\mathbf R\)-PL, shrink \(V\) once more and apply pullback stability of
\(\mathbf R\)-PL functions
\cite[Lemma~5.4(1)]{GJR26}.  For quasi-smooth \(Y\), the required
regularity is the already verified quasi-smooth P06.1 theorem.  This
proves every assertion.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of \Cref{thm:p061-split-toric-all-orbits}]
Fix \(x\in W\).  There is a unique face
\(\tau\preceq\sigma\) such that \(x\in O(\tau)^{\mathrm{an}}\).  Put
\[
 N_\tau=N\cap\operatorname{span}_{\mathbf R}(\tau).
\]
It is a saturated sublattice of \(N\), so choose a splitting
\(N=N_\tau\oplus N'\).  Choose
\[
 q\in\operatorname{relint}
 (\sigma^\vee\cap\tau^\perp)\cap M.
\]
Such an integral relative-interior point exists because the dual face is
rational polyhedral.  Since
\(\sigma\cap\operatorname{span}_{\mathbf R}(\tau)=\tau\), its zero face
on \(\sigma\) is exactly \(\tau\).  Thus \(q\) vanishes on \(\tau\) and
is strictly positive on every ray of \(\sigma\) not contained in
\(\tau\).  The principal toric open
\(D(\chi^q)\) contains \(O(\tau)\).  Its monoid is
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p061-localized-toric-monoid}
 (\sigma^\vee\cap M)+\mathbf Z(-q)
   =\{m\in M: m|_\tau\geq0\}.
\end{equation}
For completeness, the inclusion from left to right is immediate.  For
the converse, evaluate \(m\) on the finitely many primitive ray
generators of \(\sigma\).  It is nonnegative on those in \(\tau\), while
\(q\) is positive on all the others.  Hence \(m+r q\in\sigma^\vee\) for
all sufficiently large integers \(r\), which proves
\eqref{eq:p061-localized-toric-monoid}.

Dualizing the chosen lattice splitting identifies the monoid on the
right with
\[
 (\tau^\vee\cap N_\tau^\vee)\oplus (N')^\vee.
\]
Consequently there is an algebraic isomorphism
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p061-orbit-product-chart}
 D(\chi^q)\simeq
 X_{\tau,N_\tau}\times_K T_{N'},
\end{equation}
under which \(O(\tau)\) is the product of the torus-fixed point of
\(X_{\tau,N_\tau}\) and the split torus \(T_{N'}\).  Notice that
\(\tau\) is full-dimensional in \((N_\tau)_{\mathbf R}\), whether or not
it is simplicial.

Under \eqref{eq:p061-orbit-product-chart}, the point \(x\) has the form
\((a,y)\), with \(a\) the rational fixed point and
\(y\in T_{N'}^{\mathrm{an}}\).  The set
\(W\cap D(\chi^q)^{\mathrm{an}}\) is an ordinary open neighbourhood of
\((a,y)\).  Apply
\Cref{prop:p061-parameterized-toric-fixed-fibre}.  It factors \(h\), on
a product affinoid neighbourhood of \(x\), as the pullback of a
classically pluriharmonic function on a strict affinoid domain of the
split torus.  The torus is quasi-smooth, so the verified quasi-smooth
P06.1 theorem makes that function \(\mathbf R\)-PL.  Pullback stability
\cite[Lemma~5.4(1)]{GJR26} makes \(h\) \(\mathbf R\)-PL near \(x\).

Since \(x\) was arbitrary and \(\mathbf R\)-PL functions form a sheaf
\cite[\S5.2(4)]{GJR26}, \(h\) is \(\mathbf R\)-PL on \(W\).  Both \(h\)
and \(-h\) are classically psh.  On a good strict analytic space,
\cite[Theorem~4.3]{GR25Classical} identifies classical psh
\(\mathbf R\)-PL functions with semipositive ones.  Thus both signs are
semipositive, which is harmonicity in
\cite[Definition~7.2]{GJR26}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of \Cref{cor:p061-split-toric-varieties}]
A split toric variety is covered by the affine toric opens attached to
the cones of its fan.  The first assertion therefore follows from
\Cref{thm:p061-split-toric-all-orbits} and sheafiness.  In the second
assertion, transfer a classically pluriharmonic function through the
given analytic local isomorphism and apply
\Cref{prop:p061-parameterized-toric-fixed-fibre}.  The quasi-smooth
P06.1 theorem applies to the \(Y\)-factor, and pullback through the local
isomorphism returns the claimed \(\mathbf R\)-PL and harmonic germ.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of \Cref{cor:p061-toric-forms}]
Let \(\pi:X_L^{\mathrm{an}}\to X^{\mathrm{an}}\) be the scalar-extension
map.  Extension of scalars preserves classical pluriharmonicity in both
directions by \cite[Proposition~7.2(6)]{GR25Classical}.  Thus the pullback
of the given function is classically pluriharmonic on the inverse image
of the ordinary open subspace.  This inverse image is an ordinary open
subspace of the split toric variety \(X_L^{\mathrm{an}}\), so
\Cref{cor:p061-split-toric-varieties} makes the pullback
\(\mathbf R\)-PL.  Ground-field descent for \(\mathbf R\)-PL functions
\cite[Corollary~5.12]{GJR26} gives the assertion over \(K\).
Harmonicity follows, as above, from
\cite[Theorem~4.3]{GR25Classical} applied to both signs.
\end{proof}
